answer: Cap the mint: exactly S credential slots per epoch, sold by sealed second-price auction — a lagoon no headcount can widen. A slot is one quill, the key allowed to sign answers and attest; the epoch pearl (pool R) splits evenly, R/S per slot. Reward basis is slot count, not identities, so sybils must buy slots at the price honest bidders set near their worth, R/S: n keys cost n·R/S to earn n·R/S — no cheap multiplier. A ledger rule excludes non-slotted keys. Assumes live honest demand each epoch; with thin bidding a rich attacker corners the lagoon cheaply.
